upstream.role: single source of truth for design tokens
upstream.note: This module's tokens.json is a SYNCED COPY generated by IWAC-theme/scripts/build-tokens.js. The theme's palette, type ramp, radii, spacing and breakpoints are NOT mirrored here — only the module-owned encoding scales and the fallback-assertion contract are recorded. Consumption is enforced by scripts/check-theme-tokens.js (npm run lint:theme).

model-1.note: Role slot, not a model id. The id -> slot map lives only in MODEL_SLOT (charts/sentiment-atlas.js).

model-4.note: Deliberately the cyan end of the model's own gradient, darkened: its indigo end was all but slot 2, and the subjectivity trend draws every model at once.

derivedScales.name: polarite
derivedScales.purpose: AI sentiment polarity, five grades plus N/A.
derivedScales.note: The halves are derived differently on purpose: the negative half steps by HUE across two theme tokens (dE ~40 in both themes); the positive half has only --success, so it steps by lightness TOWARD --surface. Mixing toward black inverted this scale in dark mode until v1.50.0.

derivedScales.name: centralite
derivedScales.formula: var(--primary) at 100 / 75 / 50 / 30% mixed in oklab toward var(--surface); na = var(--border-light)

derivedScales.name: subjectivite
derivedScales.formula: var(--primary) at 15 / 35 / 55 / 75% toward var(--surface), then var(--primary) itself

derivedScales.name: heatmap
derivedScales.formula: var(--primary) at 8 / 28 / 50 / 75% toward var(--surface), then var(--primary) itself

consumedScales.name: series
consumedScales.consumption: Read live from document.body. Slots 1-2 alias --primary / --secondary (admin-tunable seeds); slots 3-20 read live too. The hex arrays in asset/js/iwac-theme.js are degraded-mode fallbacks only and are deep-equalled against tokens.json's `series` by lint:theme rule 11 — light and dark separately, plus leadSlots and which tokens hold the leads.
consumedScales.grammar: COUNTRY_MAP (charts/shared/chart-options.js): one country, one slot, for every chart. Benin 0, Burkina Faso 1, Cote d'Ivoire 2, Niger 3, Nigeria 4, Togo 5, Senegal 6; accented and unaccented spellings share a slot; unknown countries take the next free slot from 7 and keep it for the session. C._countryColor resolves the slot through IWACVis.getSeriesColor, which wraps.

consumedScales.name: resource type
consumedScales.consumption: Rendered as a dot on an outlined badge (.iwac-vis-badge--<type> sets --iwac-vis-badge-dot). Read at call time so a theme swap repaints without remounting the panel. The pipeline's `image` key maps to --type-photograph.

moduleLayoutTokens.name: --iwac-vis-thumb-col-lg / -md / -sm
moduleLayoutTokens.purpose: Total table-cell width for the thumbnail column (thumb + padding).

moduleLayoutTokens.name: --iwac-vis-panel-toolbar-reserve
moduleLayoutTokens.purpose: Header space reserved so a trailing badge cannot collide with the injected download / fullscreen buttons.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: The module's entire elevation budget: the panel boundary. Nothing inside a panel casts a shadow.

shadows.name: chart-tooltip
shadows.purpose: The one floating element — the tooltip is appended to body to escape ancestor overflow clipping, so it carries its own depth.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Every control state change: background, border, colour, shadow.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: false at ECharts theme level
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the chart theme disables animation globally; option builders only ever set durations, so one switch silences initial and update animation everywhere.

breakpoints.name: note
breakpoints.value: Owned by IWAC-theme and published in tokens.json. @media cannot read a custom property, so these three are literals in the stylesheet header AND asserted by lint:theme rule 10: min-width on a breakpoint, max-width at breakpoint - 1.

i18n.locale: resolved once from <html lang>; language switching in IWAC is a page navigation, so there is no runtime switch
i18n.guard: npm run lint:i18n — key parity both directions; an English-identity key is deliberately absent because t() falls back to the key

i18n.mechanism: Omeka's translator ($this->translate / @translate), catalogue in language/fr.po + committed fr.mo
i18n.guard: npm run lint:i18n-mo — Omeka loads only the .mo and the release zip is a git archive, so a reworded msgid with a stale .mo falls silently through to English

guards.name: lint:theme
guards.asserts: no removed tokens; oklab mixing only; no mixes toward black/white; no bare hex/rgb/hsl outside a var() fallback; every fallback equals tokens.json's canonical light value; no var() inside a fallback; every var(--…) names a published or module-owned token; font-size from --text-*; media widths on published breakpoints; the series arrays deep-equal tokens.json's series contract

guards.name: lint:blocks
guards.asserts: the block registry, config invokables, BlockLayout classes and templates agree — a block whose embed slug did not match its template filename 500'd every embed of it

guards.name: lint:i18n / lint:i18n-mo
guards.asserts: dictionary parity, and that fr.mo was recompiled from fr.po

components.name: Panel
components.description: The unit of the system: one chart, its title and its description, on the theme's panel ground.
components.html:
Articles per year

How many articles the collection holds for each year.
components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; background: var(--panel-bg, var(--surface, #fdfcfb)); color: var(--ink, #13161c); border: 1px solid var(--border, #ced1d6); border-radius: var(--panel-radius, var(--radius-md, 0.5rem)); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm, 0 1px 3px 0 rgba(9,11,15,0.12), 0 1px 2px -1px rgba(20,22,27,0.06)); padding: var(--space-4, 1rem); min-width: 0; font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-panel__title { margin: 0 0 var(--space-1, 0.25rem); font-size: var(--text-base, 1.0625rem); font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink, #13161c); } .ds-panel__desc { margin: 0 0 var(--space-3, 0.75rem); font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.8125rem); color: var(--muted, #66696e); line-height: 1.5; } .ds-panel__chart { height: 240px; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(to top, color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 18%, transparent), transparent); } .ds-panel__chart:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: The module's only button skin. Nothing in a data panel is the page's call to action.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: var(--space-2, 0.5rem) var(--space-3, 0.75rem); background: var(--surface, #fdfcfb); color: var(--ink, #13161c); border: 1px solid var(--border, #ced1d6); border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); font-size: var(--text-sm, 0.9375rem); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)), border-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)); } .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--surface-raised, #faf8f6); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 40%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Tab Group
components.description: Toggle buttons in a labelled group — aria-pressed, not an ARIA tablist. Active state is a tint and a border, never a filled orange.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-1, 0.25rem); padding-bottom: var(--space-2, 0.5rem); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-light, #e2e5e8); } .ds-tab { padding: var(--space-1, 0.25rem) var(--space-3, 0.75rem); background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #66696e); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: var(--text-sm, 0.9375rem); font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)), color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)), border-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)); } .ds-tab:hover { background: var(--surface-raised, #faf8f6); color: var(--ink, #13161c); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tab--active { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 12%, var(--surface-raised, #faf8f6)); color: var(--ink, #13161c); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 40%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); }

components.name: Facet Chip
components.description: Set-membership filter. Pill, primary tint, aria-pressed.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem; border-radius: var(--radius-full, 9999px); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 40%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 12%, var(--surface, #fdfcfb)); color: var(--ink, #13161c); font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.8125rem); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)), border-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)); } .ds-chip:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 22%, var(--surface, #fdfcfb)); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 60%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Form Control
components.description: One rule for every select and text input in the module, applied centrally by P.buildSelectControl / P.buildSearchDropdown.
components.css: .ds-control-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.8125rem); font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-light, #3f4349); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-control { padding: var(--space-2, 0.5rem) var(--space-3, 0.75rem); background: var(--surface, #fdfcfb); color: var(--ink, #13161c); border: 1px solid var(--border, #ced1d6); border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: var(--text-sm, 0.9375rem); transition: border-color var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)), box-shadow var(--transition-fast, 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)); } .ds-control:hover { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 40%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); } .ds-control:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Window Disclosure
components.description: A dateline, not a banner: the standing count under a windowed chart, with a text-link way out. Hidden entirely when nothing is being hidden.
components.html: Showing the top 20 of 82.
components.css: .ds-window-note { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: var(--space-2, 0.5rem); margin: 0 0 var(--space-2, 0.5rem); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-window-note__text { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.8125rem); color: var(--muted, #66696e); } .ds-window-note__toggle { padding: 0; background: none; border: 0; color: var(--primary, #ce4115); font: inherit; font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.8125rem); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-window-note__toggle:hover { color: var(--primary-hover, #b03710); } .ds-window-note__toggle:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chart Key
components.description: The module's answer to a legend printed across the bars: a flat inline list whose swatch carries the data mark's own 2px corner.
components.html:
• Benin
  • Burkina Faso
  • Côte d'Ivoire
components.css: .ds-key { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-1, 0.25rem) var(--space-3, 0.75rem); margin: 0 0 var(--space-2, 0.5rem); padding: 0; list-style: none; font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-key__item { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; color: var(--ink-light, #3f4349); font-size: var(--text-2xs, 0.6875rem); line-height: 1.4; } .ds-key__swatch { width: 0.75rem; height: 0.5rem; border-radius: 2px; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Fetch Error State
components.description: The retryable failure. A 404 never reaches this — it is routed to the quieter 'not published yet' banner, because a missing bundle is a publication state, not a fault.
components.html: This visualisation could not be loaded.
components.css: .ds-error { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: var(--space-3, 0.75rem); min-height: 160px; padding: var(--space-4, 1rem); color: var(--muted, #66696e); font-family: var(--font-body, "Public Sans", system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: var(--text-sm, 0.9375rem); text-align: center; } .ds-error__msg { margin: 0; } .ds-error__retry { padding: var(--space-2, 0.5rem) var(--space-3, 0.75rem); background: var(--surface, #fdfcfb); color: var(--ink, #13161c); border: 1px solid var(--border, #ced1d6); border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); font: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-error__retry:hover { background: var(--surface-raised, #faf8f6); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #ce4115) 40%, var(--border, #ced1d6)); } .ds-error__retry:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline, 2px solid var(--focus-color, #ce4115)); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The theme's world is The Research Broadsheet — a 20th-century newspaper operated as a scientific instrument. This module is that broadsheet's data page: the charts, tables and maps a newspaper prints when it has counted something. It inherits the whole register — density over comfort, rules as joinery, quiet controls, one accent used sparingly — and adds nothing to it. What it adds is encoding: the grammar by which a country, a sentiment grade, a resource type or an AI model becomes a colour, and the rules that keep that grammar honest when the surface flips to dark, when an admin retunes the brand seed, or when the theme is absent altogether.

The governing fact is physical: a <canvas> sits outside the cascade. Nothing in a chart can inherit. So every colour, every font stack, every axis tint is read from the live custom properties at render time and converted to a legacy rgb() the chart engine can deconstruct. That single constraint produces most of this system: the runtime token reader, the paired light/dark fallback objects, the computed-not-listed contrast rules, the theme observer that repaints instead of remounts.

The second governing fact is that this repo owns no visual identity. It owns one CSS namespace (--iwac-vis-) and one class prefix (.iwac-vis-). Everything else resolves upstream, with a guarded fallback for the degraded case. A value that looks like brand appearing in this repo is a defect, not a decision — and the token guard is written to say so out loud.
keyCharacteristics: A consumer, not an author: one namespace, one class prefix, everything else upstream
Colour is encoding, never chrome — the module's own tokens all carry data meaning
Derivations mix toward --surface / --ink, never toward black or white
Panels are the theme's sanctioned exception to flatness; everything inside them is flat
Contrast decisions are computed per theme, per call — never listed
Every consumed token carries a fallback the build asserts against tokens.json

rules.name: The No Second Palette Rule
rules.body: --iwac-vis- is for values the theme should not carry: data-encoding colour and module-local layout constants with no theme equivalent. It is not a place to re-declare a theme token. --iwac-vis-icon-btn-sm: 28px was --size-control-xs to the pixel and the shadow tints re-derived what --shadow-color* already publishes; both are gone. The guard exempts the full prefix only, so a shortened one (--iwac-otd-…) fails.

rules.name: The Mix-Toward-Surface Rule
rules.body: A derived swatch mixes toward --surface or --ink, never toward black or white. Black and white are the two colours in the palette that are not theme-relative, so a ramp built on them inverts when the surface goes dark: -sent-pos-strong was --success mixed 18% toward literal black until v1.50.0, which left the most emphatic grade on the scale as the dimmest thing on the chart in dark mode (4.96 against 8.28 for the grade below it). A theme-pinned block that already knows which way is up opts out with /* allow-absolute-mix */.

rules.name: The Role-Slot Rule
rules.body: A model accent is a position, never an identity. These tokens were once named from the Hugging Face column prefix, so every model upgrade renamed a design token and orphaned the rules referencing it. A version identifier is not a design decision.

rules.name: The Computed-Not-Listed Rule
rules.body: Which palette slots may carry text is computed from the live palette against the live --panel-bg, per theme, per call — never enumerated. Measured against the light panel 13 of 20 slots sit under 4.5:1; against the dark panel a different 5 do; there is no subset that works in both. A hardcoded list would be correct until the next palette edit and wrong silently thereafter. When nothing qualifies the code falls back to the ink token: monochrome-and-readable beats varied-and-not.

rules.name: The Live-Read Rule
rules.body: Chart colour is read through getComputedStyle and resolved to a legacy rgb() before it reaches the engine — never hardcoded, never handed over as color-mix(). The parser cannot deconstruct modern colour syntax, so a color-mix() series colour paints correctly at rest and vanishes on hover. Opacity variants go through ns.withAlpha, which emits a flat rgba() that survives the engine's own lift/darken.

rules.name: The Panel-Not-Surface Rule
rules.body: Anything measuring contrast against the box it sits in reads --panel-bg, not --surface: the theme aliases --panel-bg to --surface in light and to --surface-raised in dark. Guessing is wrong in exactly one theme, which is the hardest kind of wrong to see.

rules.name: The Charts-Inherit-The-Body-Face Rule
rules.body: The chart theme reads getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily and hands it to every axis, legend and tooltip, so canvas type never visibly clashes with the page around it. Naming a family in chart code is how every chart on the site once rendered in Inter on a Public Sans page.

rules.name: The Panel-Titles-Are-UI Rule
rules.body: Panel titles are sans-serif at --text-base/600 — they are labels above charts, not editorial headings. The serif treatment is reserved for the block-level section heading, which is what ties a block into the page's h1/h2 rhythm. Heading level is an outline decision, not a style one: buildPanel emits h4 by default, h3 under a block heading promoted to h2, h2 for a block sitting directly under the page h1 — and the level never changes the size.

rules.name: The Token-Or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: font-size comes from a --text-* token, inside clamp() included. Roughly 91 literals here once ran a second, undeclared 12/14/18px scale against the theme's 11/13/15/17/19; four inline fluid ramps hid from the guard inside clamp() until it learned to read the whole value.

rules.name: The Reserved-Height Rule
rules.body: A chart host declares its height before its data arrives. Panels that render a placeholder into the chart itself use the shared empty-chart option rather than emptying the host, so the reserved space survives an empty slice.

rules.name: The Documented-Media-Width Rule
rules.body: @media cannot read a custom property, so the three widths this module reflows at are written as literals and named in the stylesheet header — and the guard checks them against the published breakpoints, because a comment saying /* sm */ beside the wrong number is what "documented" looked like right up until it was wrong.

rules.name: The Flat-Inside-The-Panel Rule
rules.body: The panel's own shadow is the module's entire elevation budget. If a control inside a panel needs to read as raised, it is the wrong control.

rules.name: The Structural-Stripe Exception
rules.body: A border-left / border-right of 2px or more is allowed only as a structural data marker — the multi-colour sentiment-card model indicator, the compare-corpus A/B edge. As decoration on a card or callout it is banned, per the theme.

dos: Do resolve every colour, font and size from a theme token with a fallback equal to the theme's canonical light value, and let npm run lint:theme compare it.
Do read chart colours at runtime through iwac-theme.js and register charts via IWACVis.registerChart() — one theme observer repaints them all.
Do derive a new scale by mixing in oklab toward --surface or --ink.
Do compute a contrast decision from the live palette against --panel-bg, per theme, per call.
Do give every chart host role="img", a focusable tabindex, and an authored localized description that is re-applied after every setOption.
Do name a data-role token by its position when its identity can be upgraded.
Do route client-rendered strings through iwac-i18n.js and PHP strings through Omeka's translator, and recompile language/fr.mo with every fr.po edit.
Do use --focus-outline for focus, and reach for --ring-focus only where an outline would be clipped by an overflow or scroll ancestor.
donts: Don't declare a token in --iwac-vis- that the theme already publishes — that is a competing variable living legally inside the module namespace.
Don't hardcode a hex, rgb() or hsl() outside a var() fallback slot; sanctioned data-series literals carry /* allow-hex */ and are counted.
Don't mix toward black or white, or use color-mix(in srgb …).
Don't hand a color-mix() or calc() string to a chart — compose opacity with ns.withAlpha so the engine can still lift it on hover.
Don't measure contrast against --surface when the thing sits in a panel.
Don't enumerate which palette slots are readable as text.
Don't shadow anything inside a panel, or add a decorative side-stripe to a card or callout.
Don't claim the ARIA tablist pattern for a row of toggle buttons; aria-pressed in a labelled group is what the markup actually is.
Don't offer "Try again" for a 404 — an unpublished bundle is a state, not a fault.
Don't write an absolute font-size literal, inside clamp() included, or reflow at a width the theme does not publish.
Don't edit asset/css/**/*.min.css or asset/js/**/*.min.js — they are generated.
